text:
maria: pushed a tiny panel to Grafana for the mergeflow experiment — shows batch formation rate, queue depth, tokens/sec, and KV cache hit by pool. can someone eyeball for obvious anomalies?
aj: looking now. quick note: the tokens/sec calculation might be double-counting retries if we use request_count * avg_tokens. better to use emitted_tokens from the runtime metric.
mar ia: good call, switched to `sum(rate(emitted_tokens_total[1m])) by (pool)` for tokens/sec. updated query in the panel.
samir: seeing a ~35% drop in per-batch utilization around 14:22 UTC on the canary pool. queue depth spiked too. any correlated kernel switches?
olivia: yes, kernel-selection logs from the runtime show a fallback to the generic attention kernel at 14:21:58 for that pool. probably due to a new quantized model rollout.
maria: that's the model-rollout we did earlier. did we expect that kernel to hurt batching?
cheng: generic kernel has worse throughput with long contexts, lower batch fill rates. It can also increase tail latency which leads to more timeouts + retries, feeding back into queue depth.
aj: can we add a tiny heatmap linking kernel variant -> batch_utilization over time? I want to see per-variant impact.
maria: added a per-kernel timeseries and a tag filter on the panel. deploy-bot: grafana:panel/mergeflow-kernel-impact updated by maria at 2026-03-18T15:12:10Z
samir: sharing quick prom query for KV hitrate by prefix: ```sum(rate(kv_cache_hits_total{pool="canary"}[5m])) / sum(rate(kv_cache_requests_total{pool="canary"}[5m]))``` not perfect but gives trend.
olivia: KV hit drops from 82% -> 57% at the same time window. that explains higher token emission per request and lower batch reuse.
aj: hypothesis: quantized variant changed token alignment so prefixes don't match cache keys as much. can we sample prefixes at 14:20-14:25?
maria: added a short trace export for that window to S3 (path: s3://redwood-experiments/mergeflow/traces/2026-03-18-1420-1425/).
cheng: also saw an increase in kernel ISR warnings in the runtime logs: ```WARN kernel_dispatcher: fallback to scalar_attention for layer 7``` those correlate to model variant metadata (float16->int8 path).
samir: given this, propose two telemetry actions: 1) add kernel_variant tag to batch formation metrics 2) emit kv_prefix_mismatch_rate metric (counts when kv key lookup misses due to prefix mismatch)
maria: +1. I'll prototype kv_prefix_mismatch_rate using a small runtime counter and a prom exporter.
olivia: for dashboarding, suggest panels: - batch_utilization by kernel_variant, - queue_depth and queue_latency p95, - tokens/sec (emitted) stacked by pool, - kv_hitrate and kv_prefix_mismatch_rate
aj: also add an alert: if batch_utilization drops >25% and queue_depth increases >3x in 5m for a pool -> page. keeps oncall from being surprised.
maria: created an alert rule draft: ```IF (batch_utilization_pool_canary < 0.5 and increase(queue_depth_pool_canary[5m]) > 3) FOR 5m THEN page oncall```
deploy-bot: alert-rule/mergeflow-canary-batchdeg created by maria
cheng: one more ask: capture kernel_switch_count metric (labeled by from_variant->to_variant) so we can detect rollouts that cause many switches.
maria: adding that too. will run a small perf run on staging tonight and push changes.
samir: awesome. can we follow up tomorrow AM with a short postmortem if the staging run shows the same pattern? 10-15 min sync.
maria: yep. setting calendar for 10:00 UTC. thanks all :thumbsup:
aj: thanks — the new panels look useful already.
olivia: saved a copy of the dashboard and shared with platform-observability.
__notes: Slack thread: concise messages, includes inline code, bot messages, and prom queries. timestamps are root and last message times, participants are display names.
